chapters.title: Every heading is cover. Every button is a factory.
chapters.body: Bullets travel through viewport space and collide with cached text geometry. A hit writes a literal 0 or 1 into the existing DOM Text node. That letter can be consumed once, and inherits its real page font and color. Button health drains through a liquid fill. A destroyed factory stops spawning for the rest of that wave.

chapters.title: Get stronger during the fight.
chapters.body: Pulse starts with one shot. Twin unlocks at 8 XP, Trident at 24, and four-shot Overdrive at 50. Letters give 1 XP, aliens 4, factory hits 2, and a destroyed factory another 8. Fire cadence accelerates from 160 ms to 95 ms. Weapon pods appear on the interceptor as it upgrades.

chapters.title: A tiny cast, built from pixels.
chapters.body: The cyan interceptor keeps its split nose, stepped wings, lime core, and twin engines through Pulse, Twin, Trident, and Overdrive. Movement drives small thrust and banking frames. Finite pixel variants are baked once and reused with smoothing disabled; collision and firing geometry stay stable.

chapters.title: Fast shots still hit thin letters.
chapters.body: A swept segment test checks the path from the previous bullet position to the next. The nearest intersecting glyph, alien or factory wins, so a fast projectile cannot simply jump across a narrow letter between frames. Alien and bullet objects are recycled through bounded pools.

site.extra: Three shields. Four waves. Factories reactivate between waves. Chained kills build a multiplier up to ×5; losing a shield resets the combo, but keeps your weapon.

characters.name: Interceptor
characters.rules: Steer with the mouse or arrow keys. Hold Fire or Space. Shooting page text leaves real binary behind; weapon upgrades unlock at 8, 24 and 50 XP.

characters.name: Drone
characters.rules: The slowest alien shape. Spawns from live button gates and chases your ship with a sideways sway. One hit early; two from wave 3.

characters.name: Crab
characters.rules: Uses the same pursuit rules as the drone, with a higher movement speed. Contact costs a shield. Destroy its gate to stop that spawn source.

characters.name: Squid
characters.rules: The fastest of the three alien shapes. Health rises with the wave, just like the other aliens; keep moving while firing.

page.lead: Fly an interceptor through a real webpage. Shoot letters into binary, break the button factories, and clear the aliens they release over four waves. It plays right here in your browser: no install, and Recall gives the page back.
page.support: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

howToPlay.title: Press Play
howToPlay.body: The interceptor launches over this page. Buttons become alien factories, and the headings and paragraphs are the battlefield.

howToPlay.title: Fly and fire
howToPlay.body: Steer with the mouse, WASD or the arrow keys, and hold click or Space to fire. On a phone the thumbstick flies and the round Fire key shoots; hold both together.

howToPlay.title: Upgrade your gun
howToPlay.body: Combat XP upgrades the weapon during the run. Pulse starts with one shot; Twin unlocks at 8 XP, Trident at 24 and four-shot Overdrive at 50.

howToPlay.title: Break the factories
howToPlay.body: Shoot a button until its health level drains. A destroyed factory stops spawning for the rest of that wave; factories reactivate between waves.

howToPlay.title: Clear four waves
howToPlay.body: You have three shields. Finish wave four to clear the page. Press Escape or Recall at any time to give the page back.

tips.title: Shoot the text
tips.body: A letter gives 1 XP and keeps the three-second combo window open, so page text is the quickest way to the next weapon tier.

tips.title: Chain your kills
tips.body: Three chained alien kills raise the combo multiplier, up to ×5. Losing a shield clears the combo but keeps your weapon.

tips.title: Hit the factories
tips.body: A factory hit gives 2 XP and a destroyed factory another 8, and it shuts that spawn source for the wave.

tips.title: Keep moving
tips.body: The squid is the fastest alien shape, and alien health rises with the wave. G jumps to the next factory; P pauses.

items.title: No zoom mid-run
items.body: While a run is live, a pinch, an iOS gesture or a double tap no longer zooms the page out of shape. One finger still plays and drags the scoreboard; the end of the run gives the zoom back.

items.title: The scoreboard still drags
items.body: Grab it with one finger on a phone or with the mouse; the drag never zooms the page.

items.title: On Fizlet 0.20.0
items.body: Same game and rules as before; the engine underneath is the only change to Null Invaders.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything to play Null Invaders?
faq.a: No. Null Invaders plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and press Escape or Recall when you are done to give the page back.

faq.q: Can I play Null Invaders on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. Phones get a thumbstick to fly and a round Fire key, and you can hold both at once.

faq.q: What happens to the page when I play?
faq.a: Shots write a literal 0 or 1 into the page's own text, and buttons become alien factories. Recall restores what the game changed and still owns.

faq.q: Can I put Null Invaders on my own site?
faq.a: Yes. It is open source (MIT). The GitHub repository has the source code, setup instructions and integration examples.
